title: Five things our ad data showed in 2026, each with its number
hook: Five things our ad data showed in 2026. Each with its number.
caption:
Five things our ad data showed in 2026. Each with its number.
All five come from Galvor's analysis of ads launched from May to September across the brands we work with.

The short version: Meta's delivery now favours an ad that looks different from what you already run, and some ad styles need longer before you judge them.

Two limits. The analysis covers brands we work with, so treat each finding as a pattern to test in your own account. And four of the five are about spend and cost in the early weeks, which is delivery. Whether an ad sells over its life is a separate question.

Swipe for the five.
alt_text: Eight-slide carousel. Cover: Five things the ads told us in 2026. Then five stat slides: new ads that looked like many running ads got 36 percent less first-month spend; a proven message in a new look got 47 percent more; six or more look-alikes launched within three days each got 48 percent less; some ad styles start 35 percent dearer per order in the first two months; one brand's creative diversity score went from 63 to 92 out of 100. Then four moves for this quarter and a closing slide asking readers to follow Galvor.
cta: Follow Galvor; first comment points to Decoded #9 (2026 in Creative)
